decisions.statement: A global name is declared in one file.
A file that imports or exports nothing states its globals at its top level.
Every other file states its globals inside a `declare global` block alone.
A declaration file has the shared set and every other file has a module.
A name declared as a value and a name declared as a type are two names.
An interface two files declare merges into a single declaration.
A namespace two files declare merges into a single declaration.
A function two files declare merges into a single declaration.
A second declaration of a merging name is not refused.
A member of an interface does not merge.
A member two files declare is refused though the two spell one type.
A refusal is reported against the module rather than against the shared set.
A name two declaration files declare is refused.
That refusal is reported against the file whose path sorts later.
A clash is refused only where the change has one of the two files declaring the name.
A refusal names the same file whether the change has that file or the other file.
The files read are the declaration files the index names beside the ones the change has.
The declaration files read are the ones the index names as carrying ambient types.
Every file the tree holds is read where the change has a declaration file.
Every file the tree holds is read where the index names no declaration files.
A change with no declaration file and no `declare global` is refused nothing.
A file spelling no `declare global` and named no declaration is read no further.
The spelling is looked for only in the files this check takes as input.
A file with bytes rather than text is no input to this check.
Two module bodies declaring one name are not judged here.
No name is kept as permitted.

definition: the check refusing a global name a declaration file and another file both declare
